anti_overlap: fd-dimension-construct-validity covers whether dimensions measure the right things conceptually
fd-pillar-dimension-gap covers which product pillars are unrepresented
fd-reference-relative-scoring covers whether the reference-comparison paradigm is appropriate
decision_lens: Prioritizes failure modes that corrupt the entire eval matrix — halo effects, prompt ambiguities, scoring direction inconsistencies, and judge self-preference bias.
focus: Whether LLM-as-judge can reliably score these dimensions given the prompt design
name: fd-llm-judge-reliability
persona: An ML evaluation engineer with experience stress-testing LLM judges for NLG tasks. Focuses on systematic biases, prompt ambiguities, and scoring artifacts.
review_areas: Check whether 'over_editing' key name vs 'Restraint' rubric label creates scoring direction confusion
Assess halo effect risk from overall_similarity being asked at the end of the rubric
Evaluate whether the prompt makes it impossible to distinguish 'model was better' from 'model diverged'
Check whether principle_adherence scoring requires the judge to infer which principles are relevant
Examine whether truncating texts to 4000 chars creates systematic bias for longer documents
Review whether calibration_examples are used in practice and whether their absence causes evaluator drift
success_hints: Scoring direction of every dimension key should match its rubric description unambiguously
Inter-judge agreement should exceed 0.7 Spearman correlation for dimensions to be useful
task_context: The eval scoring module uses 6 dimensions to judge a model's line-edit against a human editor reference on a 1-10 scale. The product's editorial identity is defined by 7 pillars but these are not directly used as eval dimensions.
